title: Counting in binary with ones and zeros
examples: How do you count in binary?
Why do computers use ones and zeros?

items.label: 16s place
items.ask: How high can you count with five bits?

explain.say: Imagine a row of light bulbs. Each bulb can only be on or off, nothing in between. A computer is full of tiny switches just like that, so it counts with only two digits: 1 for on and 0 for off. That is called binary. Look at the bulbs on the board.

draw.text: Counting in binary with ones and zeros

items.label: 16s place
items.ask: How high can you count with five bits?

explain.say: See how each bulb is worth double the one on its right? 1, then 2, then 4, then 8, then 16. In our normal numbers each place is ten times bigger; in binary each place is two times bigger. What comes after 16?

items.label: 16s place
items.ask: How high can you count with five bits?

explain.say: Now let us count. Zero is all off. One is just the 1s bulb. Two? Turn off the 1s bulb and turn on the 2s bulb: 10. Three is both on: 11. Watch the pattern march along the board. What do you think four looks like?
Look at the 8s bulb. With four bulbs, 8, 4, 2 and 1, all on, you get 8 plus 4 plus 2 plus 1, which is 15. So four bulbs count from 0 to 15. How many bulbs would you need to reach 16?

items.label: 16s place
items.ask: How high can you count with five bits?

explain.say: Fantastic, you can count like a computer! A row of 8 bits is called a byte, and it can count from 0 all the way to 255. Challenge: hold up your fingers as bits and try to show the number 6.

faq.q: Why do computers use ones and zeros?
faq.a: Inside a computer are billions of tiny switches called transistors. Each one is either on or off, so two digits, 1 and 0, are the easiest and most reliable way to store numbers.
asks: Why do computers not use ten digits?

faq.a: Binary has only two digits, so when a place is full you carry to the next place, which is worth two of the one before. So the places go 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and so on.
asks: What are the place values in binary?

faq.q: How high can you count with five bits?
faq.a: Five bits are worth 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1. All on makes 31, so five bits count from 0 to 31: that is 32 different numbers.
asks: What is the biggest number with 5 bits?
How many numbers can 5 bits make?

faq.a: Five is 4 plus 1, so turn on the 4s and the 1s places and leave the 2s off: 101.
asks: How do you write five in binary?

faq.a: A bit is one binary digit, a single 1 or 0. The word comes from binary digit. Eight bits make a byte.
asks: How many bits are in a byte?

facts: Bit is short for binary digit.
One byte is 8 bits and can store any whole number from 0 to 255.
The German thinker Gottfried Leibniz wrote about the binary number system in 1703.

quiz.why: The 1s are in the 4s place and the 2s place, and 4 plus 2 makes 6.

wrong.1: In binary the places are 4, 2 and 1, not hundreds, tens and ones.
wrong.2: Three is 011; here the 4s bulb is on too.

quiz.say: In binary, each place is worth how much compared with the place on its right?

wrong.0: Ten times is for our normal base ten numbers.
wrong.2: If they were the same, you could not make big numbers.
